title: Fitbit and Google team up as they look to ‘transform future of wearables’
text:
Download PDF version 11:23 30 Apr 2018 Fitbit will use Google’s cloud platform so its wearable users can connect their data with electronical medical records By combining Fitbit’s data with EMRs, patients and their clinicians should be able to implement more personalized care plans
Fitbit Inc ( NYSE:FIT ) shares sprinted higher on Monday after the wearable tech group told investors it is teaming up with Google to improve its healthcare offering.
The San Francisco-based company is well-known for its smartwatches which can track users’ activity and heart rate, and it has been stepping up its efforts to integrate into the broader healthcare system. READ: Fitbit plans 'mass-appeal' smartwatch after disappointing sales
As part of today's announcement , it will use Google’s new cloud healthcare platform in order to connect users’ data with electronic medical records (EMRs).
By combining Fitbit ’s data with EMRs, patients and their clinicians can get a better understanding of their health which can help to improve care and better manage chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension.
As part of the tie-up, Fitbit will move onto the Google Cloud Perform which the company said will allow it to scale faster and remain at the forefront of technology.
“Working with Google gives us an opportunity to transform how we scale our business, allowing us to reach more people around the world faster, while also enhancing the experience we offer to our users and the healthcare system,” said James Park , co-founder and chief executive of Fitbit.
“This collaboration will accelerate the pace of innovation to define the next generation of healthcare and wearables.”
As for first-quarter results which are due later this week, Wall Street analysts are forecasting ad adjusted loss of US$0.20 a share on revenue of US$247.6mln. ‘Fitbit the ideal healthcare partner’
Craig-Hallum analyst Alex Fuhrman has said Fitbit is the “ideal healthcare partner” given its massive wealth of data, including over 100bn hours of healthcare information.
Fuhrman thinks the company's data is "significantly more valuable" than that of Apple Inc’s ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) Apple Watch because its devices have a battery life of approximately four days, allowing Fitbit users to wear the device to sleep and thus collect data continuously for 24 hours.
The analyst repeated his Buy recommendation and US$10 price target.
Fitbit shares rose 5.9% in premarket trading to US$5.60. Top stories
